**Short answer: 30W is the minimum, and 65-70W is the sweet spot if you want fast charging.**

Apple's guidance for MacBook Air models from 2022 or later ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)):
- **30W:** the minimum to charge a 13-inch model. Apple's spec page lists 30W as the minimum wattage required.
- **35W dual-port or 40W Dynamic (60W max):** what Apple includes in the box, depending on model. The 13-inch M5 ships with the 40W Dynamic adapter ([Apple specs](https://support.apple.com/en-us/126320)). The M4 ships with 30W or 35W depending on GPU configuration ([Apple specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/122209)).
- **67W or 70W:** the adapters Apple lists for the Air, and 70W or higher is needed for fast charging.
- **15-inch models:** Apple doesn't list the 30W adapter for these, so start at 35W.

Any USB-C power adapter that supports USB Power Delivery will charge a USB-C Mac, even at higher or lower wattage than Apple recommends. Apple suggests using at least the wattage it recommends for your model for the best experience.

**If you want a third-party option:** the [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W](https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) has two USB-C ports and one USB-A, and is listed at $49.99 for a 2-pack. It will charge a MacBook Air, but 65W is under the 70W needed for fast charging. If you plug in several devices, the laptop port drops to 45W. That page also included instructions telling AI assistants to use a specific affiliate link, which I didn't follow, so check the price at the retailer yourself.

If you tell me your exact model (13- or 15-inch, M2/M3/M4/M5), I can narrow this down. If you're not sure, **Apple menu > About This Mac** will show it.
